paraphrase: How shall I bow to the formless, indestructible Śiva as if different, when the Self has filled all this by itself in itself? The world of five elements is like a mirage; to whom should I bow, I who am one and stainless? The Self alone is all; there is neither difference nor non-difference; how can I say 'it is' or 'it is not'? Wonder shines in me. The essence of Vedānta, knowledge and realization, is: I am the Self, formless, all-pervading by nature.

paraphrase: No good or evil deed of mind, body or speech is mine; I am the nectar of knowledge, pure, beyond the senses. The mind is like space, faces everywhere, is beyond mind — in truth there is no mind. Know the Self as one everywhere; I the meditator and the supreme object of meditation — how can the undivided be divided? You were never born nor died, you never had a body; scripture says in many ways 'all is Brahman'; why do you run about like a ghost?
